title: Several results
description:
Write three functions that each return more than one value, or a value worked out in steps:

```lua-norun
stats(list)         -- three results: the smallest value, the largest, and the mean (average); nil for an empty list
clamp(x, lo, hi)    -- x, but no lower than lo and no higher than hi
divmod(a, b)        -- two results: a // b and a % b
```

```lua-norun
stats({ 4, 9, 2 })      --> 2, 9, 5.0
clamp(15, 0, 10)        --> 10
divmod(17, 5)           --> 3, 2
```

solution.solution.lua:
function stats(list)
    if #list == 0 then return nil end
    local lo, hi, total = list[1], list[1], 0
    for _, v in ipairs(list) do
        if v < lo then lo = v end
        if v > hi then hi = v end
        total = total + v
    end
    return lo, hi, total / #list
end

function clamp(x, lo, hi)
    if x < lo then return lo end
    if x > hi then return hi end
    return x
end

function divmod(a, b)
    return a // b, a % b
end

hints: `return a, b, c` returns three values. The caller writes `local x, y, z = f()` to take them all.
unitTests:
test("stats gives three results", function()
    local lo, hi, mean = stats({ 4, 9, 2 })
    check_eq(lo, 2)
    check_eq(hi, 9)
    check_eq(mean, 5.0)
    check_eq({ stats({ 7 }) }, { 7, 7, 7.0 })
    check_near(select(3, stats({ 1, 2 })), 1.5)
end)

test("stats of an empty list", function()
    check_eq(stats({}), nil)
end)

test("clamp", function()
    check_eq(clamp(15, 0, 10), 10)
    check_eq(clamp(-3, 0, 10), 0)
    check_eq(clamp(4, 0, 10), 4)
    check_eq(clamp(0.5, 0, 1), 0.5)
end)

test("divmod", function()
    check_eq({ divmod(17, 5) }, { 3, 2 })
    check_eq({ divmod(-7, 2) }, { -4, 1 })
    check_eq({ divmod(10, 5) }, { 2, 0 })
end)
